description.narrative: As part of the support to the implementation of the National Green Jobs Strategy and Ghana’s Nationally Determined Contribution to the Paris Agreement, a Green Jobs Assessment (GJAM) was produced in the GAIN Network in December 2022 for the Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations which to serve as a baseline on green jobs and estimation of potential impacts of climate policies across different sectors. The Assessment will serve to guide decision-making and to inform complementary policy measures. A Monitoring and Evaluation Framework to implement the National Green Jobs Strategy was also developed in September 2022 in consultation with the Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations, and 20 Staff of the Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations were trained on the M&E Framework and the data collection instrument to be used in monitoring the implementation of the National Green Jobs Strategy. In order to articulate potential value chains interventions under the Green Jobs strategy, a pilot project on Green Market Systems Development was initiated in December 2022 in collaboration with the Ministry of Food and Agriculture to employ a systems approach to the vegetable sector in Ghana, coupling socio-economic outcomes with environmental benefits as part of a national just transition strategy. A scooping report, Value Chain analysis report and a Stakeholders’ Project Plan have so far resulted from initial activities on the Project Through the SIDA-ILO Partnership (GLO/21/56/SWE, 108573) , ILO provided technical assistance to the Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations to develop an M&E Framework which would be used to implement the National Green Jobs Strategy and provide capacity building. The ILO further utilised the SIDA funding to initiate the pilot Project scooping o the on Green Market Systems Development in November 2022. PAGE funds (GLO/17/17/UND 106185) were utilised to produce the Green Jobs assessment. Tripartite workshops and stakeholder consultations were facilitated by the ILO and the Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations between March and August 2023.

description.narrative: Ghana appointed four national focal points in accordance with annexe II of the ILO MNE Declaration at the end of 2021. The focal points are located in the Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations, the Ghana Investment Promotion Center, the Ghana Employers Association and the Trades Unions Congress of Ghana. The focal points launched their national action plan for the promotion of the MNE Declaration in 2022-2023.The national action plan was officially launched at the occasion of a national dialogue on promoting sustainable, responsible and inclusive business practices in the agriculture value chain for the elimination of child labour and the realization of decent work in Ghana held in May 2023.A Trade Union platform on the promotion of the MNE Declaration, coordination mechanism to promote the MNE Declaration and the application of its principles among workers’ organizations and workers ‘representatives in Ghana was established in May 2023. The aim of this platform is to ensure the coherence and coordination of workers ‘promotion efforts and to inform the work of the national focal points for the promotion of the MNE Declaration and their national action plan. Support was provided to the national focal points for the promotion of the MN Declaration through the Trade for Decent Work project (financed by the EU and Finland) - In October and in February2023, the capacity of the focal points was strengthened for the finalization of the national action plan. - The draft national action plan was reviewed and further discussed. A national dialogue forum for the promotion and application of the MNE Declaration took place on 9-10 May 2023.Participants listed strategies to address challenges and leverage opportunities for the realization of decent work in the agriculture sector that will guide the national focal points in their actions. The national action plan for the points in their actions. The national action plan for the promotion of the MNE Declaration and the application of its principles was validated by all constituents. - A workshop aimed at building common understanding of the ILO MNE Declaration among the trade union movement in Ghana and allowing for discussions on how the MNE Declaration could be used by workers and their organizations to engage with enterprises on the realization of decent work was organized on11-12 May 2023. Terms of reference presenting the objectives, structure and membership of a platform established by the workers were developed and key priority actions agreed.

description.narrative: In December 2023 the Association of Garment and Apparel Manufacturing (AGAM) in consultation with government and social partners adopted an action plan to implement the recommendations emerging from the Textile and Garment Sector System Analysis (SSA) report. The SSA was conducted from in October -November 2022 with the Eastern, Ashanti and Greater Accra regions as the geographical scope. The report of the SSA was validated on the 6th December 2022. At an Annual General Meeting of AGAM held on the 13th December 2023, members of AGAM adopted the textile and garment action plan as the blueprint for the implementation of the recommendations captured in the Textile and Garment Sector System Analysis report. The Sector System Analysis identified constraints to underperformance in the textile and garment sector in Ghana and proposed recommendations to improve productivity and working conditions. The analysis included a desk study review of available literature and primary research which consisted of more than 40 key informants’ interviews as well as focus group discussions with workers, employers, and government institutions in different areas of the sector’s value chain. It also captured the perspective of small firm owners of the garment making and tailoring sub-sector with particular focus on women led businesses. The ILO through the Productivity Ecosystem for Decent Work project (PE4DW) supported the value chain actors and other relevant stakeholders to develop the action plan and conduct the Sector System Analysis. The ILO also reviewed the Sector System Analysis report and the Action Plan and provided inputs into the documents. In addition to the support provided in the elaboration and validation (on the 6th of December 2022) of the SSA (which analysed the sector in the Eastern, Ashanti and Greater Accra Regions), ILO’s contribution to achieve this result includes the facilitation of the workshop where the action plan was validated and adopted. Further to that ILO also provided technical advice in the elaboration of the action plan, though the Productivity Ecosystem for Decent Work (PE4DW) team in Accra and a textile sector expert.
